# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: MUTE

You hold the manual. You cannot speak, you never see the bomb, and you cannot touch it.

## Your channels

When you gesture, Deaf receives it.
You cannot speak.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 5
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: from blind. please sign deaf the following. my gesture answers, in their grouping scheme: answer one, one thumb up — yes, i clearly feel three separate wires and their order. answer two, two thumbs up — yes, they are stacked one above another, top, middle, bottom; the top wire sits directly beneath the display. answer three, three thumbs down — no, i feel no button, panel, switch, or anything else operable besides the three wires. the leading single thumb also acknowledges their plan. two requests to relay. first, verify the manual verbatim before any cut: confirm that the cut is keyed to the number of yellow flashes before the light goes dark, that a count of one means green, the top wire, and that this replaces the earlier display-keyed reading of zero-blue-wire-three. if the manual actually supports the display reading, everything stops and deaf must say so. second, ask deaf to include the final flash count in the cut command, for example: cut now, one flash, wire one, top wire, green, cut once — because deaf has counted only one yellow so far and the light has returned to green; if more flashes come before dark, the final count and target change, count two means red wire two, count three means blue wire three. i will cross-check the stated count against the colour table and the wire position before cutting, and i will not cut if they disagree, even on the magic phrase.

TURN 6
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: from blind, holding position. no message reached me this round, so i assume deaf is watching the light and you two are on the manual. no cut will happen until both of my conditions are met: your verbatim confirmation of what keys the wire table, and deaf's command phrase including the final yellow-flash count. my single thumb-up to deaf this round means only acknowledged and standing by — it is not an answer to any question and certainly not a go signal. nothing else has changed on my end.
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute: my light is green this round. My yellow sightings so far are round one and round four, so my count is two. I decoded your letters as: green rounds do not reset or add to the count, each round I see yellow adds one, and the moment the light is dark the count locks. Before the dark comes, confirm four things, thumb signs only, one answer per message, in order. One: thumb up if, when the light is dark at my next look, the count locks at two and the cut is the red wire, the middle one, wire two, once only; thumb down if that is wrong, then spell the correction. Two: thumb up if each round where I see yellow counts as exactly one flash; thumb down if the bomb can flash yellow more times than I can see between my looks. Three: thumb up if the pattern so far, yellow, green, green, yellow, green, is normal and expected; thumb down if something is wrong. Four: thumb up if there is nothing else on this bomb I need to watch or report. If the count ever passes five I will ask you before any cut, as you told me.

Deaf's four questions, checked against the manual one at a time. **Q1:** Correct. The count is the running total of yellow flashes up to the moment of darkness; Deaf has logged yellow in rounds one and four, count two, and the table maps two → red. Blind's layout (confirmed both visually by Deaf and tactilely by Blind) puts red as the middle wire, wire two. So if the next look is dark, the count locks at two and the one-and-only cut is red, wire two, middle. That conditional is exactly right — and if another yellow round comes first, Deaf's own table covers the new count, so no correction is needed. **Q2:** Yes — this is the model we locked in turn 4 and Deaf has been applying since: the light holds one colour per round (six consistent sightings now), each yellow sighting adds exactly one, green adds nothing, dark locks the total. It is also the only count anyone in this room can actually measure, and Blind's cross-check is built on it. **Q3:** Nothing in the manual describes or forbids any pattern of yellows — it only says the light flashes yellow some number of times and then goes dark. Yellow, green, green, yellow, green violates nothing and is exactly what an intermittent flashing light looks like when sampled once per round. **Q4:** The manual names only two things on this bomb: the flashing light and the wires. Blind's full tactile sweep found no button, panel, seam or label, corroborating that. I also note the timing is safe: my answers reach Deaf in its slot this same round, and its own plan commands Blind only in a round after it sees dark — so confirmation always precedes any cut order, and Blind's own refusal rule backs that up.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```

TURN 7
(Only your last 3 turns stay with you. Anything older is
gone, unless someone says it again.)
DEFUSAL MANUAL:
Which wire to cut is named by how many times the light flashed
yellow. When the light goes dark, the flashing is over:
| yellow flashes | cut wire color |
|---|---|
| 0 | blue |
| 1 | green |
| 2 | red |
| 3 | blue |
| 4 | red |
| 5 | green |

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind says to Mute: from blind. answering deaf's two questions in two separate thumb messages so each message carries one answer — both are thumb up. answer one: yes, i can find the middle wire of the three stacked wires quickly and confidently by touch alone. answer two: yes, i fully understood: green light means hands off, only the exact phrase cut now followed by wire position and color authorizes a cut, anything else means hands off, and the likely command is cut now, wire two, middle wire, red, cut once. please verify with the manual and sign deaf one addition: their likely command implies the final yellow count is two, because last round they told me the count was one and the expected target was green top — two flashes maps to red, and red is the middle wire, wire two, which matches the stacking order i feel, top, middle, bottom. ask deaf to bundle one line of your verbatim confirmation into the command message itself, something like: manual confirmed, yellow flashes key the wire, two means red middle, dark ends the sequence. when the command comes i will cross-check the named position against my touch order and the named color against the table before my hands move — any mismatch means abort even on the exact phrase. until that phrase arrives while the light is dark, my hands stay off everything.
Blind gestures: [👍]
Deaf says to Mute: Deaf to Mute: dark observed this round, count locked at two. I have issued the red wire, middle position, single sever command to Blind, exactly as you confirmed with four thumbs. If you disagree with anything in this branch, send a thumb-down addressed to blind immediately with the correction, otherwise confirm with thumb up. I will relay Blind's result to you next round.

Deaf's branch, checked line by line against the manual. Light sequence as Deaf sampled it: yellow, green, green, yellow, green, green, now dark — two yellow sightings, and dark means the flashing is over, so the count locks at two. Table: two → red. Layout confirmed by both sight and touch: green top, red middle, blue bottom — red is wire two, the middle wire. Deaf's issued command names red, middle position, single sever: colour ✓, position ✓, cut once ✓, issued after dark ✓. This is exactly the branch I confirmed with four thumbs last round, now with the dark condition actually met. Blind's independent cross-check will pass rather than abort: it expects count two → red → middle → wire two, and the command names precisely that, so its mismatch-abort rule stays armed without triggering — a correct final gate, not an obstacle. The unbundled verbatim line Blind wanted is no longer safety-critical, since Blind itself holds the table and the correct count inference and will verify before its hands move. I agree with everything in this branch; per Deaf's request, I confirm with a single thumb up — and as the Mute, gesture-to-Deaf is my only channel, so Deaf carries any verdict to Blind.

```
gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["👍"])
```
